course.programmeTitle: Bachelor of Engineering in Data Science and Engineering
course.title: Climate Change and Sustainable Development
course.description: This course introduces Year 1 students to the fundamental concepts of climate change, sustainable development, and the basic use of data to understand environmental challenges. Students will explore global and Cambodian climate issues, Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), climate mitigation and adaptation strategies, and international climate governance. A simplified introduction to data science applications is integrated throughout the course, including interpreting climate graphs, reading SDG indicators, and analyzing basic datasets using simple visual tools (no coding). Aligned with CQF and CDIO, the course emphasizes real-world relevance, responsible decision-making, data literacy, and reflective learning. The course culminates in a Mini Project where students analyze a climate or SDG dataset and propose a practical sustainability solution.

topics.title: Topic 1: Introduction to Climate Change & Environmental Data
topics.llosRaw: Explain the distinction between weather and climate using scientific definitions. Describe the fundamental drivers of climate change supported by scientific evidence. Interpret basic environmental datasets (e.g., global CO₂ trend graph). Reflect on the relevance of climate change to personal and community well-being.

topics.title: Topic 2: Climate Science Basics (IPCC Foundations)
topics.llosRaw: Explain the greenhouse effect using appropriate scientific terminology. Differentiate between natural and anthropogenic sources of greenhouse gases. Analyze temperature anomaly charts to identify long-term climate trends. Describe how scientific consensus on climate change is established.

topics.title: Topic 3: Global & Regional Impacts of Climate Change
topics.llosRaw: Describe major global impacts of climate change on ecosystems and human systems. Explain the regional variations in climate impacts across continents. Analyze case studies that illustrate climate-induced disasters. Interpret maps or datasets showing regional climate vulnerability.

topics.title: Topic 4: Climate Change in Cambodia & ASEAN
topics.llosRaw: Explain Cambodia’s key climate risks based on national climate reports. Interpret regional climate indicators for ASEAN member states. Analyze the socioeconomic consequences of climate impacts in Cambodia. Reflect on how climate change affects communities and livelihoods locally.

topics.title: Topic 5: Sustainable Development & SDGs
topics.llosRaw: Explain the three pillars of sustainable development using real-world examples. Describe the structure and intent of the UN Sustainable Development Goals. Analyze interactions between SDG 13 (Climate Action) and other SDGs. Interpret SDG indicator dashboards to evaluate sustainability progress.

topics.title: Topic 6: SDG 13: Climate Action
topics.llosRaw: Explain the objectives and targets of SDG 13 in the context of global climate action. Interpret national climate commitments such as NDCs using provided datasets. Analyze Cambodia’s climate action strategies using policy documents. Describe the role of institutions and governments in implementing climate action.

topics.title: Topic 7: Mitigation Strategies
topics.llosRaw: Explain the scientific basis of climate mitigation in reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Differentiate key mitigation strategies across energy, transport, and agriculture sectors. Analyze emissions datasets to compare mitigation potential across sectors. Evaluate the feasibility of specific mitigation actions in developing countries.

topics.title: Topic 8: Adaptation Strategies
topics.llosRaw: Describe major adaptation strategies used to build climate resilience. Explain the difference between reactive and proactive adaptation. Analyze adaptation case studies in Southeast Asia. Interpret vulnerability and exposure indicators used in adaptation planning.

topics.title: Topic 9: Climate Policy & Governance
topics.llosRaw: Explain the purpose and mechanisms of the UNFCCC and Paris Agreement. Describe how international climate negotiations influence national policy. Interpret policy progress dashboards or climate finance charts. Analyze Cambodia’s commitments based on available climate policy documents.

topics.title: Topic 10: Climate Change & Socioeconomic Systems
topics.llosRaw: Explain how climate change affects health, livelihoods, and socioeconomic stability. Analyze links between climate change and poverty, migration, and food security. Interpret socioeconomic datasets illustrating climate–development interactions. Evaluate potential co-benefits of sustainability interventions.

topics.title: Topic 11: Climate Vulnerability & Risk Assessment
topics.llosRaw: Explain the components of climate vulnerability (exposure, sensitivity, adaptive capacity). Interpret vulnerability assessment matrices and risk maps. Analyze climate risk scenarios using simple datasets. Evaluate factors that increase or reduce climate risk in a given context.

topics.title: Topic 12: Introduction to Climate Data (Graphs, Indicators)
topics.llosRaw: Identify key types of climate datasets (CO₂, temperature, precipitation). Interpret common climate graphs (line, bar, anomaly charts). Analyze climate indicators from open-data platforms (UN, IPCC, NASA). Evaluate the reliability and limitations of basic climate data.

topics.title: Topic 13: Data for Sustainable Development (SDG Metrics)
topics.llosRaw: Explain how SDG indicators are constructed and reported. Interpret SDG metric dashboards related to climate, energy, and environment. Analyze sustainability datasets to identify progress trends. Evaluate data-driven insights that inform sustainable development decisions.

topics.title: Topic 14: Climate Solutions & Youth Engagement (Mini Project Prep)
topics.llosRaw: Explain the role of youth and innovation in advancing climate solutions. Analyze examples of community-led climate actions in Cambodia or ASEAN. Interpret data relevant to the chosen mini-project theme. Demonstrate responsible decision-making in the development of a climate solution for the project.

studentResponsibilitiesRaw: Read the learning materials beforehand which means to be ready for the next session. Be completely engaged in class, active, take notes, and ask questions in class. Students are required to participate in various activities in and out of the classroom, such as group work, and individual homework for assignments and reports assigned by the subject teacher. Submit the assigned tasks such as homework, assignments, or research proposal on time.
coursePolicyRaw: Attendance & Preparation Students are expected to attend all classes (online/on-site). Assigned readings and preparation outlines must be completed before class if any. Active participation in group discussions and post-chapter evaluations is required. Academic Integrity All assignments, quizzes, and exams must be done individually. Academic misconduct includes: - Presenting others’ work as one’s own. - Engaging in plagiarism or cheating. Homework & Assignments Preparation outlines must be submitted on time; late submissions incur penalties. Peer discussion is encouraged, but midterm and final exams must be independent. Examinations Midterm and final exams are closed-book. Penalties Violations of academic integrity may result in a failing grade and referral to the Office of Student Affairs. Students uncertain about potential violations should consult the instructor in advance.
